en: The *Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī for Eliminating Premature Death*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master and Dharma Master of the Imperial Purple Robe, the Śramaṇa [Amoghavajra], at the Vaiśravaṇa Temple in the kingdom of Uḍḍiyāna in North India.
Translated by the Subject Shi Hu by Imperial Decree: Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying on the banks of the Gaṅgā River together with a great assembly, headed by the Four Great Heavenly Kings who Guard the World and the Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Four Kings, saying:
"There is a great terror that is deeply loathsome and distressing.
You should know that whether they be men or women, boys or girls, humans or devas,"
I observe that those who die prematurely experience great terror;
they are constantly disturbed and afflicted, unable to save one another,
until they reach the even greater terror of old age and death.
It is inexhaustible.
I shall now explain for you the Dharma of protection.
At that moment, within the assembly, the Four Great Heavenly Kings...
Then they addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
having heard this teaching today in the presence of the World-Honored One,
we are leaping for joy and filled with delight."
"I offer my body, life, and wealth to the Tathāgata;
I pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will expound this for me.
At that time, the World-Honored One, with a single snap of his fingers, said:
Facing east, he stood and spoke these words: "Homage to all Tathāgatas,
the Unsurpassed Perfectly Complete Buddhas of the ten directions,
who possess vast compassion and pity for sentient beings."
They have all realized *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*. We pray that you,
out of compassion, will likewise observe us and bestow your power and protection upon these sentient beings who cling to a self.
"Quell premature death and expound this teaching.
Thus did all the Tathāgatas, from the east, west, south, and north,
even to the zenith and nadir, proclaim these words.
Homage to all Tathāgatas, the Unsurpassed, Perfectly Awakened Ones,
who, without abandoning compassion,
have attained *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* for the sake of sentient beings.
I pray that you, out of compassion, will together observe me and expound this teaching for the sake of sentient beings.
At that time, may all the Buddhas together bear witness as I now proclaim the Dharma for rescuing and protecting from fear, and for pacifying and eliminating calamities.
In this way, even when the second turning of the Wheel of Dharma was being proclaimed,
all within this assembly attained fullness of lifespan and physical form;
they were all freed from the fear of birth and death and suffered no premature death.
This is likewise true even unto old age and sickness.
At that time, all the Buddhas of the ten directions perceive the forms and images of the Tathāgatas in every single world.
Pervading all things like the measure of sesame seeds,
those Tathāgatas of each of the ten directions together raised their voices and spoke this mantra:
Tadyathā | Tsale tsala tsale | Viniṣṭhite svasti kṛte | Kṣīraṇīreṇa prasphāntau | Sarvasigāriṇa ā ||

At that time, all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions...
Having spoken this secret mantra, he said these words:
"All Tathāgatas, the Unsurpassed Perfectly Enlightened Ones, all speak thus.
At that time, the Northern Heavenly King Vaiśravaṇa addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One..."
Now that I have heard of the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgatas of the ten directions supporting and protecting me,
I shall not meet with untimely death, and my fears shall be extinguished.
Facing the Buddhas, I shall now recite this mantra:
*Tadyathā | śvete śvete | ri ri ri ri* | At that time, the Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra of the East...
Then, before the Buddha, he spoke this mantra:
*caḷi caḷi svāhā*. At that time, the Heavenly King Virūḍhaka, the Lord of Increase, who was in the south, spoke this mantra before the Buddha:
*Vāri vā vā vārī.* At that time, the Western Heavenly King Virūpākṣa stood in attendance before the Buddha and also spoke this mantra:
*Mā dandi sūma sūmu sūmu.* Then the World-Honored One addressed the Four Heavenly Kings, saying:
Now, this divine mantra is witnessed and observed by all Buddhas.
If there are sons or daughters of noble family who receive and uphold it day and night, recollecting it with sincere devotion.
One will certainly attain long life without meeting an untimely death;
after the end of this life, one shall not fall into the evil realms.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who benefits sentient beings...
If one generates a mind of sincere truth and upholds, receives, reads, and recites [this],
at the time of death one will be free from all fears,
as well as from any strange portents or evil omens.
In the present life as well, they shall be free from leprosy, insanity, and various diseases;
they shall be spared the poisons of water, fire, weapons, war, pestilence, insects, and medicines;
and even all calamities such as thunder and hail shall be entirely removed.
Wherever this sutra may be located,
the Buddhas of the ten directions and all the bodhisattvas will gather there in assembly;
they shall protect this sutra, ensuring that no obstacles or difficulties arise.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who copies, adorns, protects, purifies, recites, and reads this sutra,
it is as if they have fashioned an image of the Buddha and decorated it with various ornaments.
The merit obtained will be no different. Furthermore,
if there is another person who makes offerings to the Buddhas with a focused mind free from pride,
they shall obtain auspicious blessings and have all calamities and misfortunes extinguished.
If there are those who uphold and transcribe this sutra, they will always be free from indolence;
the merit they obtain shall likewise be so.
All sages and worthies will constantly and eternally protect them, freeing them from all calamities and afflictions.
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished preaching this sutra,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings, the dragon spirits, the eight classes of beings, the asuras,
and all the great assemblies of humans and devas [rejoiced].
Having heard the Dharma, they rejoiced, believed, accepted, and practiced it.
*The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Eliminating Premature Death*.
